prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Create a second version of the childhood portrait of Jackie Leven, now completely EN FACE, while matching the approved illustration exactly in style, palette and degree of simplification.

Image 1 is the ORIGINAL childhood photograph, reproduced on a sepia book cover. This is the source of the child's actual facial identity, age and haircut. Discard all text, strips, cover design, sepia colouring and background.
Image 2 is the approved three-quarter portrait illustration. Use it for EXACT style, tonal range, crop scale, dark crew-neck clothing, brushwork and atmosphere. It is not an adult face. The new image should unmistakably belong to the same series and depict the same child.

Only requested change: rotate the head and shoulders into a genuinely straight-on frontal portrait. The face plane is parallel to the picture plane, head upright with no sideways tilt, nose central, both eyes at comparable distance from the viewer, both cheeks visible. Eyes look directly out at the viewer. Shoulders broadly face forward too. Preserve the subtle natural asymmetry of the child's eyebrows, eyes, cheeks and mouth; do not mirror one side or make an artificial perfectly symmetrical face.
Keep the same apparent childhood age, actual distinctive facial proportions, alert serious curious expression, naturally closed/slightly parted lips, short straight dark hair with an uneven blunt fringe, and dark crew-neck top. Do not turn him into a different child, idealize or prettify him, enlarge the eyes, give him an adult face or add a smile.

Preserve the drawing language of image 2: broad matte neutral-grey light and shadow shapes, expressive rough dry-brush strokes, broken contours, selective directional hatching and dark unworked spaces. No extra detail, no photorealism or smooth airbrushing, no vector-like mechanical posterization, no finely rendered hair strands. Let the child's softer facial anatomy remain believable. The directional side-light may remain slightly asymmetric to give form; en face refers to the actual head and gaze, not flat passport lighting.
Use precisely the same subdued neutral greys and almost-black anthracite #0d0f12 as image 2. No brown, warm beige, sepia, yellow, white glare, or colour tint. Face highlights remain muted middle-grey. Dark eyes, nostrils and mouth inside lighter grey planes; natural positive lighting, not a negative.
Vertical 4:5 head-and-shoulders framing with the whole crown and hair visible, centered slightly above the middle of the canvas, dark margin around the head. Same size and breathing room as image 2. Lower shoulders and chest dissolve into loose dry-brush traces and then plain anthracite. No outer border or visible sheet.
One standalone portrait, no collage, comparison layout, lettering, signature, logos, cover elements, hands, objects or background scene. The result is a frontal companion to image 2, with its exact visual character and the identity of photo 1.
status: selected by user and integrated at 1950-kirkcaldy; original three-quarter portrait preserved
